label: Recipe
title: Slow-cooked tomato beef stew
summary: Tender beef, a rich tomato sauce and a little warmth. A slow afternoon, a very good supper.
picture_style: Natural side light, warm stone and dark cookware, close view, honest food colours, no lettering.

cover.prompt: A finished rich tomato beef stew in a dark pot, tender beef chunks, carrots, a swirl of cream and chopped parsley, with bread beside it.
cover.alt: Rich tomato beef stew, ready to serve

steps.title: Coat the beef
steps.text: Toss the 1.2 kg beef with 2 tbsp flour and a good pinch of salt and pepper. Turn the pieces until lightly coated.

steps.title: Brown in batches
steps.text: Heat 3 tbsp oil in a heavy pot. Brown the beef in small batches until a deep brown crust forms, then set it aside.

note.text: Keep space between the pieces. A crowded pot steams the beef instead of browning it.

picture.prompt: Beef chunks with a deep golden brown crust in a dark heavy pot, space between each piece, close enough to judge the browned surface.
picture.alt: The deep brown crust to aim for

steps.title: Soften the vegetables
steps.text: Turn the heat down. Cook the 2 onions, 2 carrots, 2 celery sticks and 1 capsicum until soft. Stir in the 4 garlic cloves, 2 tbsp tomato paste, paprika, cumin, chilli and oregano for another minute.

steps.title: Build the sauce
steps.text: Pour in 125 ml wine and scrape up the brown bits. Add the tomatoes, 250 ml stock, 1 tbsp savoury sauce, 1 tsp sugar and 2 bay leaves. Return the beef and its juices.

steps.title: Let the oven do the work
steps.text: Bring to a gentle simmer, cover, then cook until a fork slips into the beef easily and it starts to fall apart.

note.text: For a slow cooker, cook for 8 hours on low or 4 to 5 hours on high instead.

picture.prompt: A spoon lifting fork-tender beef from thick glossy tomato sauce in a dark pot, showing how the beef separates easily and the sauce clings.
picture.alt: Tender beef and sauce that clings to the spoon

steps.title: Thicken and taste
steps.text: If the sauce is thin, uncover for the last 20 to 30 minutes until it coats a spoon. Remove the 2 bay leaves and taste before adding salt or chilli.

steps.title: Finish gently
steps.text: Take the pot off the heat. Stir through 100 ml cream and scatter the chopped parsley over the top.

note.text: Let the bubbling settle before adding cream. Do not boil it afterwards, or it may split.

blocks.title: Make tomorrow easier
blocks.text: The flavour deepens overnight. Freeze portions before adding the cream, then stir it in when you reheat the stew until piping hot.

parts.text: Creamy mash, crusty bread, rice or wide pasta. For a gentler stew, use just 1 tsp chilli flakes.
